body:
Current requirements:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **2.1.6** | Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password. | 1 | 620 |
| **3.7.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that the application requires re-authentication or secondary verification before allowing highly sensitive transactions or modifications to sensitive account attributes such as authentication settings. | 1 | 306 |

Sections:

  * V2.1 Password Security
  * V3.7 Defenses Against Session Abuse

---

Re-working the requirement levels raised the question - what level is suitable for 3.7.1?

  * "allowing highly sensitive transactions" - this is a bit abstract and feels like level 3, session takeover may allow to execute sensitive functionality
  * "modifications to sensitive account attributes such as authentication settings" - probably level 2, session takeover provides vector to take over the related account

So most likely it makes sense to split 3.7.1.

Then, watching at 2.1.6, it is also a defense against session abuse and it is not related to password security as such, although, from the functionality point of view, it is a logical place to find it. But, we don't have the year 2015 anymore, most likely application provide more authentication details than just asking for a password. 2.1.6 is saying "for modifying sensitive account attribute (password) require re-authentication (current password)"

The proposals/questions to discuss:

  * do we split 3.7.1?
  * if we split, do we merge "account mofication" part and 2.1.6?

comments.body:
I think it would be easier for a developer to see everything they need for a password reset in one section.

MFA + old/new password, and then a password reset link via a side channel. We can pull other requirements from the OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet. https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Forgot_Password_Cheat_Sheet.html 

I also think splitting 3.7.1 is smart, and I'd keep that separate for 'standard transactions' while keeping the auth/password-reset requirements in their own section.

I support splitting but I would rather not get this wrapped up in 2.1.6.

I would suggest something like:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **3.7.1** | [MODIFIED, SPLIT TO 3.7.3, LEVEL L1 > L2] Verify that the application requires re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes such as authentication settings. | 1 | 306 |
| **3.7.2** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 3.3.4] Verify that users are able to view and (having re-entered login credentials) terminate any or all currently active sessions. | 2 | |
| **3.7.3** | [MODIFIED, SPLIT FROM 3.7.1, LEVEL L1 > L3] Verify that the application requires re-authentication or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | 306 |
I think it makes sense also to clarify, what the "authentication settings" may mean, such as attributes used for authentication or (password) recovery, such as email, phone number, and MFA settings.

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **3.7.1** | [MODIFIED, SPLIT TO 3.7.3, LEVEL L1 > L2] Verify that the application requires re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes **which may affect authentication such as email address, phone number, MFA configuration, other information used in account recovery, etc**. | 1 | 306 |
| **3.7.2** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 3.3.4] Verify that users are able to view and (having re-entered login credentials) terminate any or all currently active sessions. | 2 | |
| **3.7.3** | [MODIFIED, SPLIT FROM 3.7.1, LEVEL L1 > L3] Verify that the application requires re-authentication or secondary verification before performing highly sensitive transactions or operations. | 3 | 306 |

What do you think?
